Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY1170 : Chemistry Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Determination of Hardness of water, Determination of the amount of Dissolved oxygen in water sample, Estimation of Iron content in the given Iron salt solution, Estimation of Calcium in given lime stone sample, Reaction kinetics of Hydrolysis of Ester, Kinematic viscosity of Oil by Redwood Viscometer, Partition coefficient of a binary mixture, Conductometric titration of strong acid vs strong base, Potentiometric titration of weak base vs strong acid.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6305 : Traffic Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Module 1 :

PRE-REQUISITE
Sound knowledge in Probability and Statistics. Log on to https://newmoodle.nitrkl.ac.in/login/index.php at least once.

Macroscopic and microscopic traffic flow parameters: distance headway, time headway, speed, flow, density. [6 hrs.]

Different types of traffic facilities. Design of traffic facilities. Application of Computer Programming for Simulation of traffic streams. [4 hrs.]
Module 7 :

Traffic surveys: Speed, volume, delay, origin and destination, parking. [6 hrs.]

Module 8 :

BACK UP
Video Link: https://ankctel.nitrkl.ac.in/lecture/35

Course Objective

1 .

Traffic control and operation
2 .

Design of different types of traffic facilities
3 .

Environmental impact analysis and Road user and vehicular characteristics contribution to pollution
4 .

Design procedures for traffic facilities management, maintenance and reliability

1 .

After the completion of this course, students will be able to:
CO1: Understand traffic flow fundamentals and design of traffic facilities,
CO2: Develop data base for calibration of traffic flow models,

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY4171 : Organic Compounds Preparation Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Preparation of following compounds: p-nitrobenzoic acid from p-nitrotoluene (Oxidation), benzhydrol from benzophenone (Reduction), selective reduction of p-nitroacetophenone (NaBH4/MeOH), salicyladehyde from phenol (Reimer-Tiemann Reaction), 2,5-dihydroxyacetophenone (Fries rearrangement), Quinoline (Skraup synthesis), 2-phenylindole (Fisher-indole synthesis), Indigo from o-nitrobenzaldehyde.

Course Objective

1 .

The course aims to equip students with essential laboratory skills, such as handling chemicals, using glassware, and performing common purification techniques (e.g., distillation, crystallization, extraction).
2 .

This course aims to provide the students with relevant experience in synthetic organic chemistry by synthesizing small organic compounds and characterizing them.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Students will gain practical experience in performing various organic reactions and syntheses, including the preparation of different types of organic compounds.
CO2: Students will gain practical experience in common laboratory techniques such as distillation, recrystallization, chromatography, and separation of mixtures.
CO3: Students will be able to apply their knowledge of organic chemistry to design and execute experiments, interpret results, and troubleshoot problems encountered during synthesis.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC6603 : Computer Vision { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

MODULE-I: Image formation and image models: cameras, geometric camera models, geometric camera calibration, radiometry measuring light, sources, and shading, color [4 Hours]
MODULE-II: Early Vision - Single Image: linear filters, edge detection, texture [6 Hours]
MODULE-III: Early Vision - Multiple Images: the geometry of multiple views, stereopsis [4 Hours]
MODULE-IV: Mid-Level Vision: Segmentation by clustering, segmentation by fitting a model [8 Hours]
MODULE-V: High-Level Vision: Learning to classify- classification, error and loss, Major classification strategy, Practical methods for building classifiers, Classifying Images- Building good image features, Classifying images of single objects [10 Hours]
MODULE-VI: Applications like object recognition, character recognition, face recognition, gait recognition [5 Hours]

Course Objective

1 .

To understand how an image is formed
2 .

To understand image filtering techniques
3 .

To get familiarized with image segmentation techniques
4 .

To understand how a classifier works

Course Outcome

1 .

After completion of this course, a student will be able:
1) To understand the fundamental concepts of image acquisition and image processing systems
2) To comprehend, analyze and design/ develop the spatial-domain and frequency-domain filters for various applications
3) To comprehend, analyze and design/ develop various image segmentation algorithms
4) To comprehend, analyze and design/ develop various feature extraction techniques
5) To comprehend, analyze and design/ develop various classifiers employed for recognition

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ID3304 : Industrial Robotics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Evolution of robotics. Robot anatomy – Design and control issues. Manipulation and Control – Sensors and Vision.
Coordinate frames. Mapping: Mapping between rotated frames – Mapping between translated frames – Mapping between rotated and translated frames – Description of objects in space – Transformation of vectors – Rotation – translation combined with rotation – translation of vectors – composite transformation – Inverting a homogenous transform – Fundamental rotational matrices.
Direct Kinematic Model – Mechanical structure and notations – Description of links and joints – Kinematic modeling of manipulator – Denavit-Hartenberg Notation – Kinematic Relationship between adjacent links – Manipulator Transformation Matrix.
Inverse Kinematic Model – Manipulator Workspace – Solvability – Solution techniques – Closed form solution.
Imaging components – image representation – picture coding – object recognition and categorization – visual inspection. Robot cell – design and control layouts. Industrial Applications – Material Handling, Process, Assembly, Inspection. NonIndustrial Applications.

Course Objective

1 .

Awarness on robots and its anatomy and applications

Course Outcome

1 .

The course is designed to help students to achieve the following outcomes
• Awareness on robotic systems.
• Awareness on various aspects of robot for industrial applications and their design.

19769.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6175 : Tribology and Rotordynamics Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Experiment 1: To determine the wear and co-efficient of friction of the material during sliding by using pin on disc apparatus.
Experiment 2: Study and experimentation on of Profile Meter
Experiment 3: To find the erosion rate of a given sample by air jet erosion test rig.
Experiment 4: To evaluate the abrasion resistance of composite using a dry sand abrasion tester as per ASTM G 65 standards.
Experiment 5: To determine the distribution of lubricating oil at various loads and speed of a Journal Bearing.
Experiment 6: To determine wear rate using two body abrasion test apparatus
Experiment 7. Rotordynamic analysis of rotor supported in rolling element bearings.
Experiment 8. To investigate the vibration characteristics of liquid lubricated bearings by measuring and analyzing vibration signatures using time and frequency domain analysis
Experiment 9. Prediction of expected life of a ball bearing for a corresponding load.
Experiment 10. Static and dynamic balancing of rotating masses
Experiment 11. Single and dual plane balancing using industrial high precession balancing machine

Course Objective

1 .

• Get practical knowledge on wear and friction of different materials
• Familiarize with the concept of tribology and rotor dynamics studies to understand the behaviours of rotor supported in various types of bearings.
• Get practical knowledge on various rotating machinery defects through vibration studies.

Course Outcome

1 .

• CO1: To understand prediction methodology of friction and wear parameter
2 .

• CO2: To understand use of erosion and abrasion concepts using erosion and abrasion wear test rigs
3 .

• CO3: To understand rotor dynamic behaviours of rotor supported by rolling element and oil lubricated bearings using rotor.
4 .

• CO4: To understand causes of rotor unbalance and approaches to balance it.

Essential Reading

1 .

Prasanta Sahoo, Engineering Tribology, PHI , 5th edition , 2016

2 .

Maurice L. Adams, Rotating Machinery Vibration: From Analysis to Troubleshooting, CRC Press , Taylor & Francis, 2000

6969.t: MM3103: Heat treatment of Metallic Materials
6969.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MM3103 : Heat treatment of Metallic Materials { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Objective and variables of heat treatments, Limitation of Fe-Fe3C Phase Diagram, Formation of Austenite, TTT and CCT Diagram, Types of TTT Diagram. Application of TTT Diagrams (Martempering, Austempering and Patenting). Annealing (Full, Homogenising, Spheroidisation and Stress-relieving annealing), Normalising, Comparison of Annealing and Normalising, Hardening and Tempering of plain and alloy steels, Hardening (Objective, Austenitizing temperature and Internal stresses), Quenching Mediums and Methods, Retained austenite and Defects in hardening, Tempering of steels, Aims and stages of tempering, Effects of Carbon and alloying elements, Tempering of alloy steels and Multiple tempering, Embrittlement during tempering. Thermo-mechanical treatment of alloys. Hardenability and its determination, Factors affecting hardenability. Case and Surface hardening: Carburising, Nitriding and Carbonitriding, Induction and Laser Hardening. Heat treatments of general engineering steels: Spring, Bearing steels, Tool steels, HSLA steel and Maraging steels, Dual phase steels and Stainless steels, Heat Treatments of Al-alloys, Cu-alloys and Ti-alloys. Age-Hardening: Types and sequence of precipitates, Mechanism and kinetics of precipitation. Heat-treatment defects and their rectification

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the principles and practices of heat treatments.
2 .

To follow different annealing, normalizing and hardening processes.
3 .

To understand the principles of surface hardening processes.
4 .

Heat treatments of different types of steels.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. The course integrates the implications of the right heat treatment to develop targeted properties and performances.
2. Different types of heat treatments are discussed to demonstrate their relevance to tailor properties.
3. Heat treatments and morphology are correlated with the chosen heat-treatment process.
4. Heat treatment defects management is also delivered.
5. Heat treatment can be an essential tool to optimize the properties of steel is well elucidated.
6. Selection of the right heat treatment to tailor the properties and performances is again presented.

Essential Reading

1 .

B. Zakharov, Heat Treatment of Metals, CBS Publishers

2 .

C R Brooks, Principles of the Heat Treatment of Plain Carbon and Low Alloy Steels, ASM Internationa

Supplementary Reading

1 .

3. G. Krauss,Steels, Processing, Structure and Performance, ASM International

2 .

K E Thelning, Steel and Its Heat Treatment, Butterworth
